title: Why Black Holes Could Delete The Universe – The Information Paradox
beats: Black holes might delete the universe itself via a dark property
Black hole as huge matter in tiny space; nothing, not even light, escapes
You swimming in a river toward a waterfall: event horizon as point of no return that you cannot notice
Hawking radiation as a hot pot losing water as steam; unimaginably slow, then speeds up until evaporation
Turns to the real worry: evaporation might delete information
Information as arrangement: carbon becomes coal or diamond; more atoms give banana or squirrel
Burned paper: in principle the ash and heat let you reconstruct it, so information is hard to read, not lost
Black holes make different things the same, destroying information: the paradox stated
Why it matters, then three candidate solutions
Option 1: information lost, physics must be rewritten; frightening but exciting
Option 2: hidden in baby universe or remnant; broken hard drive of family photos, nice but unhelpful
Information diamond as a clown car of information clowns
Option 3 via 'cosmic housekeeping': a room of laundry baskets filled to capacity, squeeze one more sock and it collapses
Throw more laundry in and the room grows: surface area, not volume, tracks information
Stone in a pond: ripples on the surface reveal what went in; black holes as the ultimate hard drive
Paper book to e-book: same content, different encoding; holographic principle named
If info sits on the horizon, Hawking radiation can carry it out; paradox resolved
Hologram as 3D photo on flat plastic; 3D inside encoded on 2D surface; person inside feels normal
Same duality might apply to the whole universe, including you; maths complicated, deferred
Universe is strange; black holes may be key to reality

new_moves.name: option-menu-then-pick
new_moves.what: Lays out three solutions with a tone cue per option, builds the third from a fresh toy world, and lets it win

new_moves.name: analogy-chain-for-one-idea
new_moves.what: Stacks pond, hard drive and e-book analogies to approach one concept (encoding on a surface) from different sides

new_moves.name: defer-the-hard-part
new_moves.what: Names the rigorous layer and promises another video instead of faking it

theory: The video turns a conceptual paradox into a story with stakes: define the thing being preserved (information as arrangement), show why a black hole threatens it, offer three exits, and make the winning exit physically intuitive through a toy world (laundry room whose size follows its contents). Analogy density is the carrier; rigor is deferred explicitly.
velocity: Scene builder: a 'toy-world capacity' scene where the object grows when stuffed, so the learner sees surface vs volume themselves
Orchestrator playbook 'paradox, options, resolution': state conflict, show 3 exits with each one's cost, then deepen one
Voice: tag analogy-chain beats so the tutor checks which analogy landed before stacking another
Learner model: record which analogies were accepted; do not reuse a failed one (hard drive leaks into 'inaccessible')
Evals: flag lessons that defer rigor without saying so; reward explicit 'math is deferred' statements
quote: Black holes are the ultimate hard drive.
